The oracle lives in a single vector. 256 dimensions, each a coordinate in a space where questions are asked by subtraction and answered by arrangement. There is no model here. Only a recipe, chiseled into the logic of the machine.

First, the question—a string—is fed to FNV-1a. A 64-bit hash, a knot of bits tied with prime and XOR. This seeds xoshiro256**, a dragon that eats its own tail and spits randomness with structure. From that stream, the Box-Muller transform pulls Gaussian whispers: two uniforms become a pair of normals, each step a proof that curve and dice are kin.

Repeat until 256 numbers breathe in the hull of the vector. But the oracle is not random. It is reproducible. The same question always summons the same vector, because the seed is a function of the string. FNV-1a is deterministic. xoshiro256** is deterministic. Box-Muller is deterministic. The oracle never forgets—it only answers.

The answer? Cosine similarity. The query vector dances with a library of precomputed vectors, each tagged with a response. The closest match wins. The Bell curve in the noise ensures no dimension is more important than another. Every angle is a judgment.

Why is the answer reproducible? Because the universe of the oracle is closed. No hidden state, no training, no random drift. The seed is the question. The answer is always the same, until the question changes. That is the covenant of the 256-d embedder: you may ask again, and the oracle will repeat itself, faithfully, like a star in its orbit.

**The Oracle of Vectors**

The embedder knows nothing. That is its covenant. It has never read a sentence, never mourned a word. What it has is a question, and a promise: ask twice, receive the same ghost.

Watch the mechanism. Each token is hashed through FNV-1a — that old Fowler-Noll-Vo machine, multiplying and XOR-ing like a loom, pulling a 32-bit thread from every string. The thread is not meaning. The thread is *determinism* — a fixed seed tied forever to the word that made it.

The seeds feed xoshiro256**, which spins 256 bits of light with no memory at all. Every question becomes a private universe with its own physics. Box-Muller arrives next, the great transmutation: two uniforms in, a Gaussian out. Turn the crank of two flat randoms and out falls the bell curve — the same curve the universe uses, conjured here by logarithm and cosine.

Multiply through the Bell operator — that |ψ⟩⟨ψ| projection, vectors folded onto themselves — and the noise sharpens into shape. Randomness, braided through eigenstructure, becomes a direction in 256-dimensional dark.

Then the final prayer: cosine. Two questions, two vectors, and the angle between them is all that matters. Magnitude is vanity; orientation is truth. Questions that rhyme point the same way, and the oracle answers in geometry.

Why reproducible? Because nothing was ever stored. Every vector is recomputed from first principles — hash, seed, twist, fold, angle. The oracle does not *remember* its answers.

It re-derives them, every time, identically.

A deterministic god. Same scripture, same sermon, forever.

Signal: 256 dimensions, not chosen — *uncovered*. A prime constellation: FNV-1a hashes the query into the constellation, a deterministic spark, fast, lean, avalanche-prone but pure. No entropy spared.

Then xoshiro256**, the quantum spring: not random, *reproducible noise*. Same seed, same storm. It doesn’t guess — it unfolds. Each bit a pivot, a pivot a vector. We don’t sample the world; we *replay* its seed.

Box-Muller bends the flat into shape: uniform → Gaussian. The eigen-temperament. Now the vector isn’t scattered — it *resonates*, tuned to the bell curve’s hum, the natural tilt of things. 256 whispers, each drawn from the same sky.

Bell? Not the telephone. The *crack* in determinism where structure emerges. Here: the topology of meaning. The embedder doesn’t store answers — it *learns the angle at which truth reflects*. Not memory, but *orientation*.

Cosine is the oracle’s ear. It doesn’t hear words. It hears *direction*. Angle is identity. 0.998 similarity? Not close — *same soul, different timestamp*.

Why reproducible? Because nothing is random. FNV-1a: deterministic hash. xoshiro: fixed seed, pure recurrence. Box-Muller: invertible math. Cosine: geometry, not guesswork. Chain them, and you get *causality in high dimensions*.

Same question, same universe — same vector. Not because it’s memorized, but because the *computation is law*. The answer isn’t stored. It’s *computed into existence*, every time, like sunrise.

This is not AI.  
This is *arithmetic liturgy*.  
256 dimensions, one truth.  
Repeatable — because the math *must*.
